content: The metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 can be influenced by various drugs, necessitating careful monitoring and potential therapy adjustments. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Cobicistat and Osilodrostat: Cobicistat increases osilodrostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, the osilodrostat dose should be reduced by half. 2. Darunavir and Ospemifene: Darunavir increases ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also raises ospemifene levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Oxcarbazepine and Darunavir: Oxcarbazepine decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Cobicistat and Oxycodone: Cobicistat increases oxycodone levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. A dose reduction of oxycodone may be warranted when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 5. Fentanyl and CYP3A4 Inhibitors: Co-administration requires frequent monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation. Fentanyl dose adjustments may be needed until stable effects are achieved. 6. Darunavir and Oxycodone: Darunavir increases oxycodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Cobicistat and Paclitaxel: Cobicistat increases paclitaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Darunavir and Panobinostat: Darunavir increases panobinostat levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. The starting dose of panobinostat should be reduced to 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Cobicistat and Paricalcitol: Cobicistat increases paricalcitol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 10. Cobicistat and Paroxetine: Cobicistat increases paroxetine levels through other mechanisms. Darunavir also increases paroxetine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose titration of antidepressants may be required to achieve the desired effect. 11. Pentobarbital and Darunavir: Pentobarbital decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat and Perphenazine: Cobicistat increases perphenazine levels through other mechanisms. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be needed. 13. Darunavir and Pimavanserin: Darunavir increases pimavanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. The dose of pimavanserin should be reduced to 17 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Darunavir and Pitavastatin: Darunavir increases pitavastatin levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 15. Darunavir and Pitolisant: Darunavir increases pitolisant levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 16. Cobicistat and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Cobicistat increases polatuzumab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and MMAE, which is a CYP3A4 substrate. 17. Posaconazole and Darunavir: Posaconazole increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. 18. Darunavir and Pramlintide: Darunavir decreases pramlintide effects due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Darunavir and Pravastatin: Darunavir increases pravastatin levels through an unknown mechanism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Cobicistat and Praziquantel: Cobicistat increases praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Darunavir and Prednisolone: Darunavir increases prednisolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Darunavir and Primidone: Primidone decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Darunavir and Progesterone: Darunavir increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Cobicistat and Quinidine: Cobicistat increases quinidine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 25. Darunavir and Quetiapine: Darunavir increases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Cobicistat and Rivaroxaban: Cobicistat increases rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Darunavir and Roflumilast: Darunavir increases roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Cobicistat and Romidepsin: Cobicistat increases romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Darunavir and Rosuvastatin: Darunavir increases rosuvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 30. Darunavir and Sildenafil: Darunavir increases sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions such as hypotension, syncope, visual disturbances, and priapism. 31. Cobicistat and Sirolimus: Cobicistat increases sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 32. Darunavir and Sitagliptin: Darunavir decreases sitagliptin effects due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Darunavir and Solifenacin: Darunavir increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Darunavir and Sorafenib: Darunavir increases sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Darunavir and Stiripentol: Darunavir increases stiripentol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 36. Cobicistat and Sufentanil: Cobicistat increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 37. Darunavir and Tacrolimus: Darunavir increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 38. Darunavir and Toremifene: Darunavir increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Cobicistat and Tramadol: Cobicistat increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. A decreased dose of tramadol may be required. 40. Darunavir and Trazodone: Darunavir increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose titration of antidepressants may be required to achieve the desired effect. 41. Darunavir and Temsirolimus: Darunavir increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 42. Cobicistat and Theophylline: Cobicistat increases theophylline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Darunavir and Tolterodine: Darunavir increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Darunavir and Topiramate: Topiramate decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Darunavir and Tisotumab Vedotin: Darunavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Darunavir and Tezacaftor: Darunavir increases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 47. Darunavir and Tinidazole: Darunavir increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Darunavir and Tipranavir: Darunavir increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Darunavir and Tisotumab Vedotin: Darunavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Darunavir and Tolterodine: Darunavir increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Darunavir and Toremifene: Darunavir increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Darunavir and Tramadol: Darunavir increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. A decreased dose of tramadol may be required. 53. Darunavir and Trazodone: Darunavir increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose titration of antidepressants may be required to achieve the desired effect.
